items.title: Get the court's authorization, then enroll
items.body: Confirm your court or the Fine Collection Center authorized DIP. Then pay $24.99 and confirm your details. Your 60 days started at your plea, so enroll the same day.

items.title: Work through the twelve modules
items.body: Eight hours, self-paced, no quizzes. Stop and resume whenever you like; most people finish across three or four sittings.

items.title: Pass the 25-question final
items.body: Twenty correct to pass. Unlimited retakes with different questions, no waiting period.

items.title: Get your certificate and completion form
items.body: Both emailed to you as PDFs the moment you pass, with the Department of Revenue's mailing address and your court's next step.

items.title: Send the form to the DOR, and to the court if told to
items.body: Mail the completion form to the Missouri Department of Revenue, Driver License Bureau, PO Box 200, Jefferson City, MO 65105-0200, and give the court a copy if it asked for one. Do it well inside your 60 days.

deadline.heading: You have 60 days from your plea, and the clock is already running.
deadline.body: Missouri requires the Driver Improvement Program to be completed within sixty days of the guilty plea or conviction for the points to be waived. The course is eight hours. The paperwork is one form. Sixty days is plenty if you start this week, and not if you start in week eight.
deadline.cite: RSMo 302.302; Missouri Department of Revenue, Tickets and Points.

benefits.headline: Points for the violation are not assessed
benefits.body: Under RSMo 302.302, when a court or the Fine Collection Center authorizes a driver to complete an approved Driver Improvement Program, the points for that violation are not assessed on the driver's record. The conviction itself still records.

benefits.headline: Once every 36 months, within 60 days
benefits.body: A driver may use the program to avoid points once in any thirty-six-month period, and must complete it within sixty days of the guilty plea or conviction. The court decides whether to authorize it.

benefits.headline: A form you or we send to the Department of Revenue
benefits.body: On completion you receive a certificate and the DOR completion form. The DOR's own guidance is that "you or the program may mail the completion form" to the Driver License Bureau; we email both documents to you the moment you pass, with the address on them.

faqs.q: Do I need the court's permission to use DIP?
faqs.a: Yes. The points are waived only when the court handling your ticket, or the Fine Collection Center, authorizes you to complete a Driver Improvement Program. Ask before you enroll. The course is still worth taking without authorization, but it will not change your record.
Sixty days from your guilty plea or conviction, set by Missouri. The course is eight hours; start the week you are authorized.

faqs.q: How often can I use DIP to avoid points?
Does DIP remove points that are already on my record?
faqs.a: No. It stops the points from the current violation being assessed. Existing points come off on their own: a third after one year with no new conviction, half after two years, all after three.
No. The conviction records; the points do not. Your insurer can still see the conviction.

faqs.q: How long does the course take?
faqs.a: Eight hours, self-paced. No quizzes. Most people finish across three or four sittings.

faqs.q: What is the final exam like?
faqs.a: Twenty-five questions, twenty correct to pass. Unlimited retakes with different questions and no waiting period.

faqs.q: How does the Department of Revenue find out I finished?
faqs.a: The completion form. The DOR's guidance is that you or the program may mail it to the Driver License Bureau, PO Box 200, Jefferson City, MO 65105-0200. We email you the completed form and the certificate the moment you pass. Mail it promptly and give your court a copy if it asked for one.
Yes. The certificate, the DOR form, unlimited retakes and support are inside that number. There is no processing fee and no upgraded version of the course.

faqs.q: Why are you more than the $10 courses?
faqs.a: Because a person answers the phone, the DOR form comes filled in with your certificate the moment you pass, and nothing is added at checkout. If price is the only thing that matters to you, a cheaper approved course will also satisfy the court.
Yes, in full, at any time before you complete the course. After you pass the exam and the certificate is issued, no refund is available.

faqs.q: Can I do this on my phone?
faqs.a: Yes. The course and exam work on a phone, and your progress saves the moment you leave.

finalCta.heading: Eight hours. One flat price. Sixty days that are already counting.
finalCta.body: Enroll the day your court says yes, finish over a week of evenings, and mail one form. That is the whole process.

help.q: How to get the court's authorization
steps: Contact the court handling your ticket, or the Fine Collection Center if your ticket was sent there
Ask whether you may complete a Driver Improvement Program to avoid points
If yes, note the date of your plea or conviction. Your 60 days run from that date
Then enroll
Click Start the Course on any page
Enter your name, date of birth, Missouri driver license number and contact details exactly as they appear on your license
Enter your court and citation details so they appear on your completion form
Pay $24.99 by card. Nothing else is charged
You receive a confirmation email with your login link
Open the login page and enter your email and password
Enter the code we email you
Click Continue Course to pick up where you left off
Work through the twelve modules in order
Each module has a minimum time; together they add up to Missouri's eight hours
Stop and resume whenever you like; your place is saved

help.q: How to take the final exam
steps: Finish every module first
The exam is 25 questions; 20 correct passes
If you miss it, retake it immediately with different questions. There is no limit

help.q: How to get your certificate and DOR form
steps: Both are emailed to you as PDFs the moment you pass
Download them and keep copies
Need another copy? Ask support. One free duplicate within 30 days

help.q: How to send the form to the Department of Revenue and your court
steps: Mail the completion form to Missouri Department of Revenue, Driver License Bureau, PO Box 200, Jefferson City, MO 65105-0200
If your court asked for proof, give it a copy of the certificate and form
Do both well inside your 60 days, and keep proof of mailing
help.note: The DOR's guidance is that either you or the program may mail the form. If you want us to mail it, contact support after you pass.

steps: Open the login page and click Forgot Password

The course and exam adapt to your screen
